table.name: Breeds
table.purpose: Lookup table of dog breeds, mapping a short breed code to its full breed name. Referenced by the Dogs table (Dogs.breed_code) in a veterinary-clinic database that also tracks owners, professionals, treatments, treatment types, sizes, and charges.

breed_code.name: breed_code
breed_code.description: Short unique code identifying a dog breed (e.g. ESK = Eskimo, HUS = Husky, BUL = Bulldog). Primary key of the Breeds lookup table; referenced by Dogs.breed_code.

breed_name.name: breed_name
breed_name.description: Full display name of the dog breed corresponding to the breed code.

table.name: Charges
table.purpose: A veterinary/pet-care billing lookup table: each row is a type of charge (e.g., Daily Accommodation, Drugs, Health Check) with its price. Likely referenced by Treatments or similar tables to assign costs, though no joins were detected in this sample (only 3 rows).

charge_amount.name: charge_amount
charge_amount.description: Monetary amount of the charge, in whole currency units (e.g., dollars). Values range 98–640 across the three sample rows; the unit/currency is not stated in the data.

charge_id.name: charge_id
charge_id.description: Primary key of the Charges table; unique identifier for each charge line item.

charge_type.name: charge_type
charge_type.description: Free-text category of the charge, e.g., 'Daily Accommodation', 'Drugs', 'Health Check' — consistent with a veterinary clinic/kennel billing context (matches the Dogs/Owners/Treatments tables).

table.name: Dogs
table.purpose: Registry of dogs at an animal shelter: each row is one dog, with its identity (id, name, breed, size, gender, age, weight, date of birth), shelter stay timeline (arrival, adoption, departure), abandonment flag, and the owner who adopted it. Linked to Breeds, Sizes, Owners, and Treatments. The data appears synthetic (random timestamps, inconsistent age vs date_of_birth, weight not matching size).

abandoned_yn.name: abandoned_yn
abandoned_yn.description: Boolean flag indicating whether the dog was abandoned (1) or not (0); 3 of 15 dogs are flagged as abandoned. Likely corresponds to dogs with no owner/adoption.

age.name: age
age.description: Age of the dog in whole years (1–9). Note: values do not consistently match date_of_birth (e.g. dog 7: age 2 but born 2017-09, ~0.5 years at arrival), so age appears to be stored independently and may be approximate or unreliable.

breed_code.name: breed_code
breed_code.description: Code identifying the dog's breed; foreign key to Breeds.breed_code (ESK=Eskimo, HUS=Husky, BUL=Bulldog).

date_adopted.name: date_adopted
date_adopted.description: Timestamp when the dog was adopted. All 15 rows have a value and each is unique, ranging 2018-02-25 to 2018-03-25, shortly before date_departed.

date_arrived.name: date_arrived
date_arrived.description: Timestamp when the dog arrived at the shelter, ranging 2017-04-15 to 2018-01-17; always before date_adopted/date_departed.

date_departed.name: date_departed
date_departed.description: Timestamp when the dog left the shelter. All values fall within a single ~20-hour window (2018-03-24 19:12 to 2018-03-25 15:05), which suggests it may actually record a data-extraction/snapshot moment rather than true individual departure times; the intended meaning is the dog's departure date.

date_of_birth.name: date_of_birth
date_of_birth.description: The dog's date of birth (2008–2018). Time-of-day components are present, indicating synthetic or auto-generated data. Does not always agree with the age column.

dog_id.name: dog_id
dog_id.description: Primary key of the Dogs table; unique identifier for each dog (1–15). Referenced by Treatments.dog_id.

name.name: name
name.description: The dog's given name; unique across all 15 rows.

owner_id.name: owner_id
owner_id.description: Foreign key to Owners.owner_id, the person who adopted the dog. Some owners (e.g. 14 with 3 dogs, 3 with 2) adopted multiple dogs. The Owners lookup's label column is a phone number, so no owner names are available here.

size_code.name: size_code
size_code.description: Code for the dog's size class; foreign key to Sizes.size_code (SML=Small, MED=Medium, LGE=Large).

weight.name: weight
weight.description: The dog's weight, a decimal value between 1.39 and 9.8. The unit is not stated; values are low for dogs, so kilograms (or another small unit) is plausible, but the unit cannot be confirmed. Also does not correlate with size_code (e.g. a 'LGE' dog weighs 1.72), suggesting the values may be synthetic.

table.name: Owners
table.purpose: Contact and address registry for dog owners in a veterinary/dog-care database; each row is one owner, linked to their dogs via Dogs.owner_id.

cell_number.name: cell_number
cell_number.description: Owner's mobile phone number, stored as free-formatted text with various formats (parentheses, dots, dashes, extensions).

city.name: city
city.description: Owner's city of residence (part of the mailing address).

home_phone.name: home_phone
home_phone.description: Owner's home/landline phone number, stored as free-formatted text with various formats and extensions.

owner_id.name: owner_id
owner_id.description: Primary key identifying each owner; referenced by Dogs.owner_id (each dog belongs to one owner).

state.name: state
state.description: Owner's U.S. state of residence (part of the mailing address), written without spaces (e.g. 'NewYork', 'NorthDakota').

street.name: street
street.description: Owner's street address including house number, street name, and unit/apartment/suite where applicable.

zip_code.name: zip_code
zip_code.description: Owner's U.S. ZIP code (5-digit, stored as text with leading zeros preserved).

table.name: Professionals
table.purpose: Staff directory of a veterinary clinic: one row per professional (veterinarian or other employee) with contact and address details. Each professional is referenced by the Treatments table, which records which professional performed each treatment on a dog. The role_code distinguishes veterinarians from non-veterinary employees.

cell_number.name: cell_number
cell_number.description: Mobile phone number of the professional, stored as free-formatted text with varied punctuation and extensions.

home_phone.name: home_phone
home_phone.description: Landline/home phone number of the professional, stored as free-formatted text with varied punctuation and extensions.

professional_id.name: professional_id
professional_id.description: Primary key of the Professionals table; unique integer identifier for each staff member. Referenced by Treatments.professional_id, indicating which professional performed each treatment.

role_code.name: role_code
role_code.description: Job role of the professional within the veterinary practice: 'Veterenarian' (veterinarian, misspelled) or 'Employee' (other staff).

state.name: state
state.description: U.S. state of the professional's address (full state names, sometimes without spaces, e.g. 'NorthCarolina').

street.name: street
street.description: Street portion of the professional's mailing address; values often embed a second line with city, state and partial ZIP, so the field holds a multi-line address block rather than a pure street name.

zip_code.name: zip_code
zip_code.description: U.S. ZIP code of the professional's address (5-digit numeric values stored as text).

table.name: Sizes
table.purpose: Lookup table of dog size categories (Small, Medium, Large), used to classify dogs (referenced by Dogs.size_code), likely for size-based pricing of charges or treatments in this veterinary/grooming database.

size_code.name: size_code
size_code.description: Primary key code for the dog size category: SML = Small, MED = Medium, LGE = Large. Referenced by Dogs.size_code.

size_description.name: size_description
size_description.description: Human-readable label of the size category (Small, Medium, Large), one-to-one with size_code.

table.name: Treatment_Types
table.purpose: Lookup table of treatment/service types offered for dogs in a veterinary/dog-care database, referenced by the Treatments table.

treatment_type_code.name: treatment_type_code
treatment_type_code.description: Short code identifying a type of treatment/service performed on dogs (EXAM, VAC, WALK). Primary key of this lookup table; referenced by Treatments.treatment_type_code.

treatment_type_description.name: treatment_type_description
treatment_type_description.description: Human-readable description of the treatment type (e.g. 'Physical examination', 'Vaccination', 'Take for a Walk').

table.name: Treatments
table.purpose: Fact table recording individual treatment events for dogs: which dog received which type of treatment, performed by which professional, when, and at what cost. Each row is one treatment event, linking Dogs, Professionals, and Treatment_Types.

cost_of_treatment.name: cost_of_treatment
cost_of_treatment.description: Cost charged for the treatment, in whole currency units (e.g. dollars); ranges 139–945 with a median of 429. Currency is not determinable from the data.

date_of_treatment.name: date_of_treatment
date_of_treatment.description: Timestamp (stored as text) of when the treatment was performed; all values fall in Feb–Mar 2018.

dog_id.name: dog_id
dog_id.description: Foreign key to Dogs.dog_id identifying the dog that received the treatment.

professional_id.name: professional_id
professional_id.description: Foreign key to Professionals.professional_id identifying the professional (e.g. vet or handler) who performed the treatment.

treatment_id.name: treatment_id
treatment_id.description: Primary key of the Treatments table; unique identifier for each treatment event.

treatment_type_code.name: treatment_type_code
treatment_type_code.description: Foreign key to Treatment_Types.treatment_type_code; code for the type of treatment: EXAM = Physical examination, VAC = Vaccination, WALK = Take for a Walk.
